newsitem.title: UK: British guards may be stripped of bear necessities.
newsitem.headline: British guards may be stripped of bear necessities.

text.p: Canada's brown bears may be spared the indignity of ending up on the heads of British soldiers under a government move to phase out the traditional bearskin hat, the Financial Times reported on Wednesday.
Animal-loving Defence Minister Lord Gilbert has told the army to look urgently at synthetic alternatives to the present headgear, known as the busby, the newspaper said.
But regiments wearing the bearskin hats feared fake fur could prove to be a sartorial disaster because previous experiments had made them a laughing stock, it added.
"When it rained the hats became rather bedraggled -- like a bad hair day," the newspaper quoted an army spokesman as saying.
"They were also subject to static electricity, which was rather embarrassing when they passed under pylons."
The Financial Times said regiments such as the Grenadier, Coldstream and Scots Guards had worn busbies since the battle of Waterloo in 1815.
The raw material for the headgear, which has made the guards a major tourist attraction, comes from the Canadian brown bear and the fur is then dyed black.

"It is a fact that Lord Gilbert has a personal interest in animal rights issues, and he has asked the army to provide the rationale for the use of bearskins," a Defence Ministry spokesman told the Financial Times.
